parsed_entries.requirement: The Appellate Tribunal must specify the matters and places in relation to which it may exercise jurisdiction.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Check if the Appellate Tribunal's jurisdiction is clearly specified in the document.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the requirement that the Central Government specify the jurisdiction of the Appellate Tribunal.

parsed_entries.requirement: Any person aggrieved by an order made by a controller or adjudicating officer may prefer an appeal to the Appellate Tribunal having jurisdiction in the matter.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Verify that the document allows for appeals to the Appellate Tribunal as per the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the right of appeal to the Appellate Tribunal under the IT Act 2000.

parsed_entries.requirement: No appeal shall lie to the Appellate Tribunal from an order made by an adjudicating officer with the consent of the parties.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Check if the document specifies that appeals cannot be made with the consent of the parties.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the restriction on appeals with the consent of the parties under the IT Act 2000.

parsed_entries.requirement: Every appeal under Section 57(1) must be filed within forty-five days from the date of receiving the order, with the possibility of extension if sufficient cause is shown.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Verify that the document specifies the 45-day filing period for appeals and the possibility of extension.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the time limits for filing appeals under the IT Act 2000.

parsed_entries.requirement: The Appellate Tribunal must send a copy of every order made by it to the parties to the appeal and to the concerned Controller or adjudicating officer.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Check if the document requires the Appellate Tribunal to send copies of its orders to the relevant parties.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the requirement to send copies of orders to the parties under the IT Act 2000.

parsed_entries.requirement: The Appellate Tribunal must have the same powers as a civil court under the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908, for certain matters.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Verify that the document specifies the powers of the Appellate Tribunal as per the Code of Civil Procedure, 1908.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the grant of civil court powers to the Appellate Tribunal under the IT Act 2000.

parsed_entries.requirement: Every proceeding before the Appellate Tribunal shall be deemed a judicial proceeding for the purposes of certain legal provisions.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Check if the document states that proceedings before the Appellate Tribunal are deemed judicial proceedings.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the classification of proceedings before the Appellate Tribunal as judicial under the IT Act 2000.

parsed_entries.requirement: The appellant may either appear in person or authorise legal practitioners or officers to present their case before the Appellate Tribunal.
parsed_entries.checkable_test: Verify that the document allows for legal representation before the Appellate Tribunal.
parsed_entries.applicability: Applicable to platforms subject to the IT Act 2000.
parsed_entries.notes: This obligation is derived from the right to legal representation before the Appellate Tribunal under the IT Act 2000.
